history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Build buggy and fixed xarray revisions identically on CPython 3.11 as pure-Python source-tree installs, then run the developer test test_polyval_timedelta_nat so it fails on buggy (NaT becomes about -1.84e19 instead of NaN) and passes on fixed. Environment (E_B, E_F) is changed only through build and dependency choices; the test is not edited.
assumptions: Recipe is 'pure': xarray is a pure-Python package with no C/Cython extensions, so the 'native_library_failure' diagnosis (compiler/BLAS named in build output) does not apply and is not acted on; if a build fails, revisit this.
No PR date is stated, so no date-based numpy pin is applied; numpy is taken as the newest release resolvable, matching the reporter's numpy 2.4.6 era.
The current interpreter was not checked; python_version 3.11 is taken from environment.language_version (3.11.13).
The developer test sits in a class or at module level; -k with the file path is used per the task instructions, so the class name is not needed.
The sentinel -1.84e19 comes from int64 min cast to float64, which is independent of numpy minor version, so the buggy behaviour is expected on the chosen numpy.

actions.step: Rebuild buggy revision as pure-Python editable install on CPython 3.11 with no pins, so numpy and xarray stay at the newest releases resolvable, as the reporter used numpy 2.4.6.
Rebuild fixed revision identically (pure, CPython 3.11, no pins) so the comparison is like for like.
Run the developer test on the buggy revision; expect an AssertionError on actual.values[1] being NaN, not a collection or import error.
Run the same developer test on the fixed revision; expect it to pass.
